label: Likely R

key_factors: Republican-leaning district (R+10 baseline lean) with incumbent David Joyce seeking re-election
Overwhelming financial advantage for Joyce: $3.1 million cash on hand versus about $34,000 for Maria Jukic

model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Republican incumbent David Joyce: a district leaning ten points Republican, a two-term incumbency edge, and a cash advantage of roughly 90-to-1 over Democrat Maria Jukic, with no outside spending on either side. Prediction markets agree, pricing Joyce near 96 percent, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin of about fourteen points Republican.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Jukic within single digits, or significant outside spending entering the district, would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican David Joyce seeks another term in this northeastern Ohio district, which leans about ten points Republican at the baseline. Joyce has built a large financial edge, holding roughly $3.1 million on hand after raising $1.4 million, while Democrat Maria Jukic has raised about $62,000 and holds only $34,000. No outside groups are active on either side.

There is no public general-election polling and no expert ratings for the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets give Joyce about a 96 percent chance of winning. The seat remains firmly in the Republican column, with modest uncertainty from the absence of direct polling.
